title: Why Most Pencils Have Six Sides ✏️

shots.vo: Look at almost any pencil, and it has six flat sides.
shots.prompt: close-up of a yellow hexagonal pencil lying on a wooden desk, vertical composition, bright warm light, highly detailed
shots.negative: text, letters, words, numbers, logo, watermark, brand name, signs, lettering, writing

shots.prompt: a round pencil rolling across a tilted desk toward the edge, vertical composition, bright warm light, highly detailed
shots.negative: text, letters, words, numbers, logo, watermark, brand name, signs, lettering, writing

shots.vo: But put a round one down on a sloping desk, and it rolls right off the edge.
shots.prompt: a round pencil falling off the edge of a school desk, motion, vertical composition, bright warm light, highly detailed
shots.negative: text, letters, words, numbers, logo, watermark, brand name, signs, lettering, writing

shots.vo: Flat sides stop it rolling, and they give your fingers something to grip.
shots.prompt: a hand holding a hexagonal pencil, fingertips on its flat sides, close-up, vertical composition, bright warm light, highly detailed

shots.vo: Six sides also let factories cut more pencils from the same slab of wood, with less waste. So check the pencil on your desk:
